The dictionary file

Source: R/dict.R
dict_file.Rd

The project dictionary is dict.yml at the project root: a YAML mapping from key to entry. An empty file, or one holding only comments, is a dictionary with no keys. A chapter's own entries are written in its front matter under weft: / dict_local:, in the same form with a why (see below); dict_local is not allowed in _weft.yml.

Details

Each entry has these fields; any other is an error, and so is a mistake in any of them. All the problems in a file are reported together.

  • value (required): by type, see below.

  • type (required): one of number, quantity, year, date, string, labels, breaks.

  • definition (required): a string that is not blank; it is the text the glossary shows.

  • unit: a string, for a quantity only.

An empty field (term: with nothing after it) is read as absent. A one-item list where a string or number is wanted (unit: [m]) is read as its item.

  • display: one unit, for a quantity only (rule 4.2.7): the unit to show the value in. The value is read in unit and converted to display when the file is read, so dict$key is already in display, and arithmetic, checks, # and units::drop_units() see it. A display that does not parse, or that unit does not convert to, is a problem; unit = at the use converts back. A ladder of units (a string with |, or a list of more than one item) is a problem: write the ladder in a unit key where the value is printed (unit="m|km", rule 4.4.23), so that the unit an entry is held in never depends on its value. A list of one item is that unit.

  • decision: a whole number from 1, or a string that is not blank; it is not resolved when the file is read. "#12" is read as 12; text such as 012, 0x1F or 1e3, or a number with more digits than an issue number can have, is kept as written and does not resolve.

  • why: a string that is not blank, for a dict_local entry only, where it is required.

  • term: a string that is not blank, on any type: the words a reader knows the entry by. dict_glossary() heads the entry with it and dict_vale() keeps it as the entry's spelling (rule 4.7.3). White space around it is trimmed; a term that holds a line break, or that starts with what markdown reads as a block (#, >, -, *, + or : and a space, 1., a fence), is a problem.

  • avoid: one string, or a non-empty list of strings, none blank, in dict.yml only (rule 4.7.4). They are spellings dict_vale() replaces by the entry's canonical spelling: its term, or, for a string entry with no term, its value; any other entry needs a term. A spelling that is the entry's own, is listed twice, is listed by another entry, or is found as whole words inside any entry's canonical spelling is a problem, and so is a spelling that starts or ends with a character that is not a letter or digit (Vale matches at word boundaries and could never match it). The entries columns term and avoid hold NA and character(0) where absent.

A key is a valid R name (make.names(key) == key) that is not reserved (..1 and ... are refused) and is not file. A whole number written with a leading zero, or in hex or octal (010, 0x1F, 0o17), is an error: write it in decimal. A merge key (<<) is an error, and so is a file of more than one YAML document; anchors and aliases without a merge key are allowed. A whole number too large for an integer is a number (a double), but under year is still an error. In a document's front matter, dict_local keys that YAML reads as booleans (yes, on, true) should be quoted if two of one truth value are used in one map, since knitr and Quarto read the front matter before weft does.

typevalueread as
numbera number, or a string that is a number literala double
quantityas number, with unita units value
yeara whole number from 1000 to 9999a weft_year: an integer, printed with no thousands mark
datea string YYYY-MM-DDa Date
stringa string (quote a number)a character string
labelsa non-empty mapping of label to phrasea lookup() function
breaksa non-empty list of itemsa brk() function

A breaks item is a mapping with a phrase and at most one of below (the value is less than the bound) or at_most (less than or equal to it); the bound is a number, .inf or -.inf. Only the last item may have no bound, and then it takes every value left. Bounds may not decrease, and a bound may not repeat the one before it so that no value is left for its band (at_most: 1 then below: 1, or equal bounds of one kind). A bound may be a number written in a string, as number may.

YAML is read so that yes, no, on, off, true and false stay as text. A duplicate key is an error.

core_len:
  value: 0.5
  type: quantity
  unit: m
  definition: "Length of each sediment core."
trend_word:
  value:
    - {below: 0.95, phrase: "a fall in"}
    - {at_most: 1.05, phrase: "steady"}
    - {phrase: "a rise in"}
  type: breaks
  definition: "Wording for the ratio of this year's mean to last year's."
